intro: Today’s picks showcase AI gateways, agent tooling, data pipelines, and eye‑catching generative demos.

picks.name: antirion
picks.what: One‑binary Rust AI gateway with console to route, secure, budget, and observe every LLM call across OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock and more.
picks.why: Provides builders a fast, unified way to manage LLM usage and guardrails without stitching together multiple services.
picks.signal: 234 stars since 17 Oct, written in Rust

picks.name: Basedash Scheduled CSV Exports
picks.what: Ask once and receive a fresh CSV in Slack or email on a weekly schedule.
picks.why: Lets businesses automate recurring data delivery without writing custom scripts or cron jobs.

picks.name: Lampline
picks.what: Build AI phone agents locally and test changes with an AI caller, importing Dialogflow CX, with optional API‑key usage.
picks.why: Enables developers to prototype and iterate on voice agents without incurring cloud costs.
picks.signal: 171 stars since 19 Oct, written in Python

picks.name: Wan2.2 14B Preview
picks.what: Generate a video from an image using a text prompt.
picks.why: Shows a compelling new multimodal capability that creators can experiment with directly in the browser.

picks.name: Corgi
picks.what: A terminal multiplexer that displays multiple AI agents’ activity, feeds, and lets you jump to the next unread agent.
picks.why: Improves ergonomics for power users juggling several agents in a single console.

picks.name: Agent Hunt
picks.what: Live rankings of the tools AI agents use most.
picks.why: Provides investors a quick pulse on which agent frameworks are gaining traction.

picks.name: Argus
picks.what: Open‑source security platform to protect against agentic attacks.
picks.why: Offers builders a dedicated solution to harden AI systems against malicious autonomous behavior.
